intro: Cincinnati owns the AFC North, Detroit lost its best pass rusher in Munich and Denver keeps winning the close ones. Thursday night brings Colts at Texans to open Week 11. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Bengals beat Steelers 38-18 and take the AFC North lead
top.dek: Cincinnati won its fifth straight and moved into sole possession of first place. The Bengals have scored 30 or more points in five straight games, a first in franchise history.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lions fear Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL
top.dek: Hutchinson hurt his right knee after a first-quarter sack in Munich. NFL Network reports an ACL tear, and an AP source says the injury ends his season, with more tests due on the meniscus.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs piles up 252 yards in Munich
top.dek: Gibbs ran for 153 yards and caught passes for 99 more, with two touchdowns. He had 171 scrimmage yards by halftime in the Lions' 35-10 win.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 16: Denver's NFL-record run of one-score wins
top.dek: The Broncos' win at Carolina stretched their streak of regular-season victories in one-score games to 16, the longest in league history. Sean Payton says the close wins are not an accident.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Colts visit Texans on Thursday night to open Week 11
top.dek: Indianapolis is at Houston on Thursday, Nov. 19 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Colts beat the Texans earlier this season and are chasing a sweep.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills roll to best start since 1991

stories.text: Bills beat the Jets 31-12 and sit at 8-1
stories.summary: Buffalo won at MetLife Stadium on Sunday and is 8-1 for the first time since 1991. Josh Allen ran for two touchdowns and threw a 45-yard score to DJ Moore. The Bills are 5-0 on the road this season.

stories.text: Secondary takes hits in New York
stories.summary: Christian Benford left with a groin injury after coming in questionable with a wrist problem. Offensive coordinator Joe Brady said Benford could still play Sunday, tracked day by day. Dee Alford was ruled out with a head injury, and LB Dorian Williams did not finish with a calf problem. Safety Cole Bishop missed three snaps with shoulder soreness and said he expects to be fine.

stories.text: James Cook runs for 157 on 18 carries
stories.summary: Cook carried 18 times for 157 yards against the Jets, including a 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. It put the game away after a close first half.

stories.text: 325: Josh Allen's career touchdowns
stories.summary: Allen now has 325 regular-season touchdowns: 233 passing, 90 rushing and 2 receiving. That passes Peyton Manning for the most through a player's first 10 seasons.

stories.text: Dolphins visit Orchard Park Sunday
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts Miami on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Bills face a Dolphins team that sits at 1-8 and starts a backup quarterback. Watch the cornerback depth if Benford and Alford are limited.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins cut kicker after 24-22 loss

stories.text: Dolphins cut Zane Gonzalez after a one-score loss
stories.summary: Miami lost 24-22 at Indianapolis and released kicker Zane Gonzalez on Monday after he missed two field goals and an extra point. Coach Jeff Hafley said the team has not decided whether to sign one of about six kickers who auditioned or hold more workouts. Daniel Carlson went 12 for 12 in his workout last week.

stories.text: Willis on IR, defensive line thinned
stories.summary: Quarterback Malik Willis is on injured reserve with a core muscle injury and will miss at least four games, including Buffalo. Surgery is possible but not decided. DT Zeek Biggers hurt a knee and DT Jordan Phillips left with an arm in a sling. Zach Sieler is out for the season with a torn biceps, and center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol.

stories.text: Rookie CB Chris Johnson takes one to the house
stories.summary: Johnson returned an interception 59 yards for a touchdown against the Colts. It was his second pick of the season. He also had a pass breakup and tackles for loss.

stories.text: 1 for 3: Miami's kicker on field goals
stories.summary: Gonzalez made one of three field goals and one of two extra points in a two-point loss. Miami also failed a two-point try after a missed extra point and trailed by two at the end.

stories.text: Miami heads to Buffalo as a big underdog
stories.summary: The Dolphins visit the 8-1 Bills on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Kyle McCord starts again at quarterback after his first career start, and Miami needs a kicker before kickoff.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye out indefinitely heading into bye

stories.text: Maye expected out indefinitely with ankle injury
stories.summary: Drake Maye hurt his ankle on the 10th play of the 35-10 loss to Detroit in Munich, and a league source says he is out indefinitely. The team fears a fractured right ankle, which is not confirmed. Coach Mike Vrabel said he would not imagine Maye being available after the bye. Tommy DeVito is the expected starter.

stories.text: Brown hamstring, Henderson on IR
stories.summary: Receiver A.J. Brown left the Lions game with a hamstring injury. Running back TreVeyon Henderson is on injured reserve, and tackle Morgan Moses missed snaps with a knee injury. Maye may need surgery.

stories.text: Tommy DeVito steps in for Maye
stories.summary: DeVito went 12 of 24 for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception against the Lions, and the offense had seven three-and-outs. Vrabel said he is confident in DeVito and does not expect to seek more quarterback help. Rookie Behren Morton would be the backup.

stories.text: 494: yards the Patriots defense allowed
stories.summary: Detroit's 494 total yards were the most New England has allowed this season. In each of the last four games, all losses, the defense gave up 400 or more yards and 30 or more points.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then the Chargers
stories.summary: New England is off this week. The Patriots visit the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 29, then face Buffalo, Minnesota and Kansas City. Watch who plays quarterback and how healthy the receiver room is.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets hope Geno Smith avoided major injury

stories.text: Geno Smith avoids major ankle injury
stories.summary: An MRI on Monday showed no major damage to Smith's ankle, and he and the Jets are hopeful he plays Sunday at the Chargers. He left the Bills game twice, first for a concussion check and then with the ankle injury. Coach Aaron Glenn said Smith is the starter.

stories.text: Cooper's ankle trouble, Smith's status
stories.summary: Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. aggravated an ankle injury early against Buffalo. Smith is hopeful to return from his ankle injury for the Chargers game. Running back Breece Hall missed five weeks earlier with a quad injury.

stories.text: Rookie Cade Klubnik makes his NFL debut
stories.summary: Klubnik, a fourth-round pick, went 11 of 20 for 137 yards with one interception in relief, and ran three times for 26 yards. Glenn said he will not play Klubnik just to evaluate him. Will Levis is the third-string quarterback on the practice squad.

stories.text: 9: straight quarters without a touchdown
stories.summary: The Jets went nine quarters without a touchdown after losing 31-12 to Buffalo. Jason Sanders's four field goals accounted for all 12 points. It was New York's fifth straight loss.

stories.text: Jets travel to face the Chargers
stories.summary: New York plays at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX. Watch the quarterback situation and whether the offense can find the end zone.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens skid to five straight losses

stories.text: Ravens drop fifth straight and sit 3.5 games back
stories.summary: Baltimore lost 23-20 to the previously winless Chargers on Monday night and fell to 4-6. Los Angeles led from start to finish. The Ravens trail first-place Cincinnati by 3.5 games with seven to play, and coach Jesse Minter says they have a two-game stretch before the bye to stay alive.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson out on IR with a broken thumb; two more starters hurt
stories.summary: Jackson fractured and dislocated his right thumb on Nov. 1, had surgery and is expected to miss six to nine weeks. He has told teammates he plans to return this season. Against the Chargers, right guard Vega Ioane left with a shoulder injury and tackle Nnamdi Madubuike left with a hamstring injury. Minter had no update on either.

stories.text: Brissett throws for 340 in his Ravens debut
stories.summary: Jacoby Brissett arrived in a trade from Arizona a week earlier and threw for 340 yards with an interception against the Chargers. Derrick Henry scored twice, and Mark Andrews led all receivers with 82 yards.

stories.text: 16: rushing yards for Baltimore on 15 carries
stories.summary: The Ravens ran for 16 yards against the Chargers, who ran for 160 on the other side. Henry found the end zone twice, but the ground game gave Baltimore no help in the loss.

stories.text: Ravens visit Carolina Sunday with Brissett under center
stories.summary: Baltimore plays at the Panthers (4-5) on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Carolina snapped a three-game skid with a 20-17 win over New Orleans. The Ravens then go to Houston on Nov. 29 before their Week 13 bye.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals own the AFC North lead

stories.text: Bengals beat Steelers 38-18 for fifth straight win
stories.summary: Cincinnati took sole possession of first place in the AFC North with Sunday night's win at Paycor Stadium. The Bengals have now scored 30 or more points in five straight games, a first in franchise history.

stories.text: No new Bengals injuries reported after Steelers win
stories.summary: Postgame coverage of the 38-18 win did not list any Cincinnati injuries. The Bengals travel to Washington on a short week for Monday night, so Wednesday's first practice report is the one to check. The Commanders' injury report was not yet posted at last check.

stories.text: Burrow throws for 409 and four touchdowns
stories.summary: Joe Burrow went 35-of-44 with four touchdowns and a 135.7 passer rating against Pittsburgh. He is the second player after Peyton Manning with four or more total touchdowns in five straight games. Ja'Marr Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards.

stories.text: 12-of-12: Burrow against Pittsburgh's blitzes
stories.summary: Next Gen Stats had Burrow perfect against the blitz in the win. He has 20 touchdown passes over the last five games, a mark only Tom Brady and Peyton Manning have reached.

stories.text: Bengals at Commanders on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Cincinnati plays at Washington (3-5-1) on Monday, Nov. 23, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Burrow faces Jayden Daniels in a matchup of LSU Heisman winners. Washington leads the all-time series 6-5-1.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns rest at 6-4 in a playoff spot

stories.text: Browns rally from 17-0 to beat Texans on a late score
stories.summary: Cleveland beat Houston 27-24 on Sunday after trailing 17-0 in the first half. Quinshon Judkins ran in the winning 5-yard touchdown with 53 seconds left. The Browns are 6-4 and hold the AFC's No. 7 seed heading into the bye.

stories.text: Watson back from concussion and leads the comeback
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson missed Week 9 with a concussion and returned to start against Houston, finishing 25-of-40 for 312 yards. The recap listed no new Browns injuries, and the bye gives the roster two extra weeks of rest.

stories.text: Watson delivers his sixth game-winning drive
stories.summary: Watson threw for 312 yards, ran for a 6-yard score and hit Jerry Jeudy on a 65-yard completion. He led his sixth go-ahead fourth-quarter drive of the season. Judkins finished it with the winning run.

stories.text: 6: wins by four points or fewer, an NFL first
stories.summary: Cleveland is the first team to win its first six games by four points or fewer. Each of those wins came after the Browns were tied or trailing with four minutes left.

stories.text: Browns on bye, then the Raiders on Nov. 29
stories.summary: Cleveland is off in Week 11. The Browns return home to face the Raiders (4-6) on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET. ESPN Analytics raised their playoff odds from 12% to 23% after the Texans win.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers lose guard McCormick in rout

stories.text: Steelers fall 38-18 in Cincinnati and lose the division lead
stories.summary: Pittsburgh dropped Sunday night's game to the Bengals and now sits behind them in the AFC North at 6-3. Aaron Rodgers opened with eight straight incompletions and finished 15-of-29 for 143 yards, mostly late. The Steelers ran for 62 yards on 17 carries.

stories.text: Guard Mason McCormick carted off with an ankle injury
stories.summary: McCormick went down late in the second quarter and left with an air cast on his right ankle. Coach Mike McCarthy declined to give details. McCormick had made 39 straight starts, and Spencer Anderson is expected to replace him at left guard.

stories.text: Metcalf supplies the late spark
stories.summary: DK Metcalf caught two long passes in the fourth quarter that covered 54 of Rodgers' 143 yards. Pat Freiermuth also scored in the fourth, but the game was long decided.

stories.text: 3: sacks of Rodgers by Cincinnati
stories.summary: The Bengals sacked Rodgers three times, including the third-down play where Jonathan Allen drove McCormick into the quarterback. The pressure fed a stalled offense that managed 143 passing yards.

stories.text: Steelers at Eagles Sunday at 1 p.m.
stories.summary: Pittsburgh visits Philadelphia (2-7) on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The game was moved to the earlier window as a Salute to Service game. The Steelers need to settle their interior line after McCormick's injury.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans blow 17-point lead, playoff hopes thin

stories.text: Texans blow a 17-point lead in Cleveland and fall to 3-6
stories.summary: Houston led by 17 and lost 27-24 when Deshaun Watson drove the Browns downfield for the go-ahead score with under a minute left. The Texans scored seven points on their last eight possessions, with six three-and-outs in the second half. Playoff hopes are fading after deep runs in each of DeMeco Ryans' first three seasons.

stories.text: Al-Shaair goes to IR as Lassiter, Marks miss practice
stories.summary: Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair went on injured reserve with a groin injury and will miss at least four games. Henry To'oTo'o takes over as the defensive signal-caller. Cornerback Kamari Lassiter (wrist) did not practice Tuesday, and Woody Marks is out of practice with a concussion. David Montgomery was estimated as a full participant after four games out and is expected back.

stories.text: Stroud has 19 TDs and 3 picks but went quiet in Cleveland
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud has thrown 19 touchdown passes against three interceptions this season. Against the Browns he finished with 211 yards, 190 of them in the first half and only 21 in the second. He was held to 167 yards and one touchdown in the earlier loss to Indianapolis.

stories.text: 33: Houston's sacks rank second in the NFL, yet the defense sits 20th
stories.summary: The Texans have 33 sacks, second most in the league. They still rank 18th in points allowed and 20th in total defense. Al-Shaair, who had 68 tackles, is the latest starter to go down.

stories.text: Thursday night rematch with the Colts
stories.summary: Houston hosts Indianapolis on Thursday, Nov. 19 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Colts beat the Texans earlier this season and are chasing a sweep. Watch whether Montgomery returns and how the secondary holds up with Lassiter's wrist in question.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts snap skid, Jones sticks as starter

stories.text: Colts end five-game skid, but Daniel Jones draws boos
stories.summary: Indianapolis beat Miami 24-22 to stop a five-game losing streak. A strip and fumble return for a touchdown by Adetomiwa Adebawore gave the Colts the lead, and Miami missed three kicks. Daniel Jones went 11 of 22 for 108 yards with two interceptions, and coach Shane Steichen said he will start Thursday.

stories.text: Both starting corners sit out of practice
stories.summary: Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee) were listed out of Tuesday's practice for a second straight day. Both left the Miami game in the third quarter. Tackles Bernhard Raimann (concussion) and Jalen Travis (knee) were also listed out.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor sits one yard from 10,000 scrimmage yards
stories.summary: Taylor carried 16 times for 83 yards and caught two passes for 20 against Miami. That left him at 9,999 career scrimmage yards. The Colts ran for 172 yards as a team.

stories.text: 12: Jones leads the league in interceptions
stories.summary: Daniel Jones threw two more picks against Miami and now has 12 on the season, most in the NFL. Steichen backed him as the starter, but a bad night in Houston could bring a change before Week 12.

stories.text: At Houston on Thursday night, going for a sweep
stories.summary: The Colts visit the Texans on Thursday, Nov. 19 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. They already beat Houston once this year. Watch the corner spots, where Gardner and Ward are questionable.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars roll Titans, lead division by four

stories.text: Jaguars beat Titans 40-23 for six wins in seven games
stories.summary: Jacksonville moved to 7-2 and leads the AFC South by four games. They have won a franchise-record five straight over Tennessee. New trade arrivals Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis were inactive, and Davon Godchaux played. Coach Liam Coen said the team played well without them.

stories.text: Hainsey and Striggow hurt, Tuten plays through foot issue
stories.summary: Center Robert Hainsey hurt his left knee and defensive end Danny Striggow was evaluated for a concussion. Neither returned, and both are listed questionable for the Giants. Running back Bhayshul Tuten played through a foot and ankle issue for a second straight week.

stories.text: Parker Washington posts career-high 152 yards
stories.summary: Washington caught seven passes for 152 yards and a 2-yard touchdown against Tennessee, both career highs. Nine Jaguars caught passes, and Coen praised the depth of the group.

stories.text: 352: Trevor Lawrence's yards, and 20,000 for his career
stories.summary: Lawrence went 25 of 35 for 352 yards and three touchdowns. He became the eighth-youngest player to reach 20,000 career passing yards, at 27 years and 40 days. He has topped 300 yards in three of his last five games.

stories.text: At the Giants on Sunday
stories.summary: Jacksonville visits the New York Giants (5-3-1) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS at MetLife Stadium. Watch the center spot if Hainsey is out.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans commit to Ward as losses pile up

stories.text: Titans fall to 1-8 and lean into Cam Ward's audition
stories.summary: Tennessee lost 40-23 to Jacksonville, its third straight loss and fifth straight at home. The team has committed to Ward as its starter, and the offense has averaged 27.6 points over the three losses. A loss Sunday would clinch a fifth straight losing season.

stories.text: Skoronski to IR, Tate and Robinson in question
stories.summary: Left guard Peter Skoronski went on injured reserve. Receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) was expected back at practice, along with linebackers Cody Barton and Anthony Hill Jr. Safety Tony Adams (concussion) and receiver Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) were still being evaluated, and all five are listed questionable for Dallas.

stories.text: Cam Ward: 716 yards, four TDs in three losses
stories.summary: Ward has thrown for 716 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions over the last three games. The offense uses more hurry-up and lets him check into plays. Against Jacksonville he hit Elic Ayomanor on a 50-yard catch-and-run and found Daniel Bellinger for a 2-yard score.

stories.text: 459: Yards Jacksonville gained, third straight game at that level
stories.summary: The Titans have allowed at least 459 yards three games in a row, after giving up no more than 399 in their first six. The defense is missing four starters to trades and injuries.

stories.text: At Dallas on Sunday, then Jacksonville again
stories.summary: Tennessee visits the Cowboys (4-6) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at AT&T Stadium. Dallas lost a 46-40 shootout to San Francisco last week, so watch the Titans defense. The Titans then face Jacksonville again.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos return from bye on a five-game streak

stories.text: Broncos come off the bye at 7-2 and hosting Las Vegas
stories.summary: Denver has won five straight and enters the second half tied for the most wins in the NFL. The Broncos beat Kansas City, Jacksonville and Seattle on the way to 7-2. Sean Payton's teams are 3-0 in the first game after a bye.

stories.text: Waddle and Moss need to clear concussion protocol
stories.summary: Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss both left the win over Carolina with concussions. Reporter Mike Klis said Waddle and receiver Marvin Mims could clear protocol before the Raiders game. Safeties Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and Brandon Jones (hamstring) sat out against Carolina, with optimism they return after the bye. This is the status as of the Panthers game, and no post-bye practice report was confirmed.

stories.text: Nix steadies the offense with two touchdowns in Charlotte
stories.summary: Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns in the 26-21 win at Carolina, including a 26-yard score to Pat Bryant in the fourth quarter. He converted six of 10 third downs, a season best. Nik Bonitto then ended it with a strip-sack and recovery with 1:24 left.

stories.text: 16: straight one-score wins, an NFL record
stories.summary: Denver's win at Carolina stretched its run of regular-season victories in one-score games to 16, the longest in NFL history. The Broncos are also 3-2 on the road this season with three straight road wins. Payton said close wins keep falling their way and that is not by accident.

stories.text: Raiders visit Empower Field on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET
stories.summary: Denver hosts Las Vegas (4-6) on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 PM ET on CBS. Raiders tight end Brock Bowers has 17 catches for 212 yards and two touchdowns in four career games against Denver, and he is day-to-day with an ankle injury. Payton wants better run blocking and better defense on third-and-long.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Mahomes throws five TDs as Chiefs reach 7-2

stories.text: Mahomes throws five touchdowns in a 35-13 win at Atlanta
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes went 22 of 35 for 348 yards and five touchdowns with no interceptions, a week after an elbow scare against the Jets. Kansas City improved to 7-2 and sits tied with Denver atop the AFC West. The defense had three sacks, six tackles for loss and nine passes defended.

stories.text: Wiley likely done with a broken ankle, Smith in protocol
stories.summary: Andy Reid said tight end Jared Wiley appears to have fractured his ankle, which will likely end his season and send him to injured reserve. Guard Trey Smith is in the concussion protocol. Travis Kelce left briefly and returned, and cornerback Mansoor Delane was pulled as a precaution after landing on his back and shoulder.

stories.text: Rookie Emmett Johnson runs for 101 in his first start
stories.summary: With Kenneth Walker III out with a groin injury, fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson carried 22 times for 101 yards and caught six passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns. It was his first career 100-yard game. Reid said when a kid comes in and he's good, you know he's good.

stories.text: 332: Mahomes passes Manning on a milestone list
stories.summary: Mahomes now has 332 career touchdown passes, regular season and playoffs combined. That passes Peyton Manning for the most by any quarterback through his first 10 seasons. The win also pushed Kansas City past its total from last season.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Arrowhead on Sunday at 1 PM ET
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts Arizona on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 PM ET on CBS. Watch the health of the offensive line and tight end room, since Smith is in protocol and Wiley is likely lost for the year. Walker missed the Atlanta game and his status is the other thing to track.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders lose Mendoza's first start, drop to 4-6

stories.text: Raiders fall 21-13 to Seattle in the Mendoza era opener
stories.summary: Las Vegas dropped to 4-6 and has lost six of its last seven. Rookie Fernando Mendoza made his first start after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota. The Raiders led 10-7 at the half, then punted on seven straight possessions and went 0-for-7 on third down after the break.

stories.text: Bowers day-to-day with a right ankle injury
stories.summary: Tight end Brock Bowers hurt his right ankle on the opening drive against Seattle, returned in the second quarter, then was ruled out for the second half. Coach Klint Kubiak called him day-to-day and said it is not as bad as first thought but still significant. He did not say if Bowers will play at Denver.

stories.text: Mendoza shows legs, but takes six sacks in debut
stories.summary: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards and ran for a 10-yard touchdown on his first drive. Seattle sacked him six times, and analysts point to trouble spotting slot pressure. The Denver game will be his first road start.

stories.text: 0-for-7: Raiders on third down in the second half
stories.summary: Kubiak called the second-half third-down failure unacceptable. After a Matt Gay field goal in the second quarter, the Raiders punted seven straight times and gained 24 yards over that stretch. Seattle scored 14 points on scramble-drill touchdowns in the same game.

stories.text: Raiders visit Denver on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET
stories.summary: Las Vegas plays at Denver (7-2) on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 PM ET on CBS. The Broncos led the league in quarterback pressures entering Week 10, a tough draw for a line that gave up six sacks. Watch Bowers' status and whether the run game, held to 65 yards, gets going.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers finally win, 23-20 over Baltimore

stories.text: Chargers end 331-day winless streak with 23-20 win at Baltimore
stories.summary: Los Angeles beat the Ravens on Monday night for its first win of the season. The last win came Dec. 21, 2025, against Dallas. Their 0-8 start was the worst since 2000. Jim Harbaugh said he was thrilled and wants to do it every week.

stories.text: Patched-up offensive line starts three rookies
stories.summary: No new injuries came out of the Baltimore win. The Chargers' offensive line has been hit hard this season and started three rookies on Monday night. Details on this week's practice designations were not available from a source I could confirm.

stories.text: Hampton hits 105 yards for his first 100-yard game
stories.summary: Omarion Hampton carried 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown, his first 100-yard game this season. Justin Herbert added 51 rushing yards, including a 22-yard touchdown, and threw no interceptions. Los Angeles ran for 160 yards, a season high.

stories.text: 0: first-half rushing yards allowed to Baltimore
stories.summary: The Ravens had no rushing yards in the first half, the only NFL team held to zero in a half this season. Derrick Henry finished with 10 carries for 10 yards, though he scored twice. Baltimore ended with 16 rushing yards on 15 carries.

stories.text: Jets visit SoFi Stadium on Sunday at 4:05 PM ET
stories.summary: Los Angeles hosts the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:05 PM ET on Fox, the first of two straight home games. The team is on a short week. Watch whether the run-heavy formula and the takeaway-free offense hold up with the line still thin.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Dak's five TDs wasted in 46-40 loss

stories.text: Cowboys waste Dak's five touchdowns in 46-40 shootout loss to 49ers
stories.summary: Dallas led 17-16 at halftime, then lost the second half 30-24. San Francisco piled up 584 yards, the most the Cowboys have ever allowed at home. Dallas has yet to win back-to-back games this season.

stories.text: Bland and Booker out, Ferguson questionable against Tennessee
stories.summary: Cornerback DaRon Bland and Tyler Booker are out. Tight end Jake Ferguson, Jonathan Mingo, Juanyeh Thomas, P.J. Locke and Donovan Ezeiruaku are listed questionable. Ferguson's status is the one to watch for the passing game.

stories.text: George Pickens returns from injury with 11 catches, 145 yards, three scores
stories.summary: Pickens came back and immediately became Dak Prescott's top target against San Francisco. Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns, tying his career high. CeeDee Lamb added 72 yards and a score.

stories.text: 584: yards the 49ers gained, a Dallas home record against
stories.summary: San Francisco averaged 9.4 yards per play and ran for 214 yards at 7.4 a carry. Christian McCaffrey had 223 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns. Dallas sacked Brock Purdy five times and still could not slow him.

stories.text: Titans visit AT&T Stadium Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Dallas hosts Tennessee at 1:00 PM ET on FOX. The Cowboys are looking for their first winning streak of the year. Prescott ranks third in the league with 2,724 passing yards and is tied for third with 21 touchdowns.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lose Thursday thriller, fix returner spot

stories.text: Giants fall 24-21 to Commanders on Diggs touchdown with 57 seconds left
stories.summary: New York lost its Thursday night home game after getting the ball back twice in the final six minutes and gaining no first downs. J.J. McCarthy threw a career-high 293 yards, but Rasul Douglas intercepted him in the last minute. The Giants stay on top of the NFC East at 5-3-1, two games ahead of Washington.

stories.text: Giants cut Charlie Jones and sign Xavier Gipson at returner
stories.summary: Braxton Berrios went down for the season, and Jones took over returns for six games. He fumbled a kickoff against New Orleans and a punt at Philadelphia, and the Giants released him Monday. They signed Gipson off the Eagles practice squad.

stories.text: Isaiah Likely catches nine for 127 yards and a 66-yard score
stories.summary: Likely was targeted 11 times against Washington and delivered the fourth-quarter touchdown that put New York ahead. Across both games against the Commanders this season he has 20 catches, 221 yards and three touchdowns.

stories.text: 3.0: sacks for rookie Arvell Reese against Philadelphia
stories.summary: Reese had 12 tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble in the 19-11 win over the Eagles on Nov. 8. He is the only NFL rookie since 2000 with 12 tackles and three sacks in one game. The Giants had seven sacks as a team.

stories.text: Jaguars come to MetLife Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Jacksonville is 7-2 and the Giants are 5-3-1. The Giants also come off extended rest after two games in five days. Watch whether the offense can keep drives alive, since it gained no first downs on its last two possessions Thursday.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles at 2-7 with Hurts out for the season

stories.text: Eagles reset after bye with Hurts out and Jordan Davis traded
stories.summary: Philadelphia is 2-7 and has lost seven straight since a 2-0 start. Jalen Hurts is on injured reserve with blood clots in his lungs and is expected to miss the rest of the year. The Eagles also sent Jordan Davis to Jacksonville for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-rounder.

stories.text: Smith and Wicks expected back soon, Hurts on IR
stories.summary: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) sat out the Giants game and are expected back soon. Hurts remains on injured reserve. The team waived Hollywood Brown and Fred Johnson and added Zach Ertz and John Ojukwu to the active roster.

stories.text: Joe Milton still learning the offense after first start
stories.summary: Milton started the 19-11 loss to the Giants on Nov. 8. He said he is learning every day, and the team has not named a Sunday starter. The Eagles say they want to put him in favorable situations and lean on Saquon Barkley.

stories.text: 7: straight losses for the Eagles
stories.summary: Philadelphia has scored 148 points and allowed 221. It is 1-4 at home and 1-3 in the division, and sits 3.5 games behind the first-place Giants.

stories.text: Steelers visit the Linc Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is 6-3 and just lost 38-18 at Cincinnati. The Eagles then play at Dallas on Thursday, Nov. 26 at 4:30 PM ET on FOX. Watch who starts at quarterback.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders rally past Giants, host Bengals

stories.text: Commanders beat Giants 24-21 on Diggs' late touchdown
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard score with 57 seconds left, and Rasul Douglas intercepted J.J. McCarthy to seal it. Washington is 3-5-1 and two games behind New York. The Commanders have not won two straight this season.

stories.text: McLaurin out for the year, Okonkwo briefly left Thursday
stories.summary: Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon against San Francisco on Oct. 19 and is out for the season. Tight end Chig Okonkwo left the Giants game for a short time. No other new injuries came out of the game.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels throws three touchdowns despite two interceptions
stories.summary: Daniels went 23 of 33 for 249 yards and ran for 28 more against the Giants. Both interceptions came in the fourth quarter, and he still drove Washington to the winning score.

stories.text: 80: career touchdown catches for Stefon Diggs
stories.summary: Diggs reached 80 with the 32-yard winner. He finished with six catches for 83 yards on 10 targets.

stories.text: Bengals visit Monday night, 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Cincinnati is 7-2 with five straight wins. Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns against Pittsburgh, and Ja'Marr Chase had 11 catches for 231 yards. Washington's secondary faces a hard test after allowing big plays to the Giants.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears come off the bye with a brutal stretch ahead

stories.text: Williams says he has moved on from the four-pick game
stories.summary: Caleb Williams threw four interceptions in the 27-24 win over Tampa Bay, two of them in scoring range. He called one throw a dumb decision and says he has put it behind him. The Bears are 7-2 and tied atop the NFC North, and six of their last eight opponents are current playoff teams.

stories.text: Gordon, Burden and Monangai all trending toward Saints game
stories.summary: Kyler Gordon (left arm) sat out Monday's practice, but the paper says it is too early to worry about Sunday. Luther Burden practiced Monday after a concussion, and Kyle Monangai (toe) practiced and is expected back for the first time since Oct. 4. Tyrique Stevenson's thumb did not keep him off the field.

stories.text: Booker has a career-high five sacks and counting
stories.summary: Austin Booker has five sacks and six tackles for loss, both career highs. Fox 32 lists him and Devin Bush as the defenders who have improved most as the season has gone on. The defense bailed out the offense against the Buccaneers.

stories.text: 6 of 8: Bears face playoff teams in six of their last eight
stories.summary: The Sun-Times calls it the NFL's toughest remaining schedule by opponent winning percentage. That run includes a Thanksgiving game at Detroit. Caleb Williams enters it with a 68.7 completion percentage, third in the league.

stories.text: Saints visit Soldier Field Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Bears host New Orleans (3-6), which the Sun-Times says has one of the league's worst defenses. Williams has a sore hamstring but has been cleared. Watch whether he avoids the turnovers that nearly cost Chicago against Tampa Bay.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions win five straight, then lose Hutchinson

stories.text: Lions beat Patriots 35-10 in Munich for fifth straight win
stories.summary: Detroit gained 494 yards, 191 on the ground, and held New England to 151 total yards. Jared Goff threw for 303 yards and three touchdowns. The Lions are 7-2, in a first-place tie with Minnesota and Chicago.

stories.text: Hutchinson reportedly tore his right ACL
stories.summary: Aidan Hutchinson hurt his knee after a first-quarter sack of Drake Maye. NFL Network reports an ACL tear, and an AP source says the injury is season-ending, with more tests due on the meniscus once the team is home. Linebacker Jack Campbell is already on injured reserve with a neck injury.

stories.text: Gibbs piles up 252 yards in Munich
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and caught passes for 99 more, with two touchdowns. He had 171 scrimmage yards by halftime. Amon-Ra St. Brown added 98 yards and two touchdowns on four catches.

stories.text: 1,384: Gibbs sets Lions record for scrimmage yards through nine games
stories.summary: No Lions player has had more through nine games in a season. The team also has 134 plays of 10 or more yards, most in the NFL. The defense has allowed 14.4 points per game during the five-game win streak.

stories.text: Buccaneers visit Ford Field Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tampa Bay comes in at 3-6. Detroit must replace Hutchinson's pass rush. The Lions have 32 sacks, third in the league.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers stew over 30-10 loss during bye

stories.text: LaFleur says protection was bad, but no staff changes
stories.summary: Green Bay lost 30-10 to Minnesota at Lambeau Field and gave up eight sacks. Matt LaFleur called the pass protection pretty bad and said some of his play calls should have been different. Offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich and line coach Luke Butkus stay.

stories.text: Parsons has a few hurdles left before Rams game
stories.summary: Micah Parsons, out since a left knee ACL and meniscus tear last December, has had his 21-day practice window opened. LaFleur says the plan is a return in Week 12, but the team reassesses at week's end. Guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) lost his first start to a practice injury, and Skyy Moore's ankle needs more evaluation.

stories.text: Love absorbs eight sacks in Minnesota loss
stories.summary: Jordan Love went 17 of 27 for 220 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He took a dozen hits, and Minnesota pressured him on 21 of 35 dropbacks.

stories.text: 57: first-half yards for the Packers offense
stories.summary: Green Bay finished with 220 total yards and went 3 of 10 on third down. It did not score until trailing 20-0 late in the third quarter. Four turnovers fed the Vikings' lead.

stories.text: Bye Sunday, then at the Rams on Nov. 25
stories.summary: Green Bay is off in Week 11 and plays at the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 7 p.m. on Netflix. Both teams are 6-4. Watch whether Parsons makes his season debut.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Cousins returns and Vikings sack Love eight times

stories.text: Cousins comes back by trade and beats the Packers 30-10
stories.summary: Kirk Cousins returned to Minnesota via trade last Tuesday and started Sunday at Lambeau Field. He threw for 207 yards on 31 attempts, and the Vikings rushed for over 100 yards for the first time in three weeks. They are 7-2 and share the NFC North lead.

stories.text: Addison needs thumb surgery and may go to IR
stories.summary: Jordan Addison hurt his thumb catching passes in practice last Friday and was inactive Sunday. Kevin O'Connell expects him out about a month, with Week 15 against Detroit the earliest return if he goes on injured reserve. Jauan Jennings is out with a calf injury, and Odell Beckham Jr. is back on the practice squad.

stories.text: Smith picks off Love for 41st career interception
stories.summary: Harrison Smith moved to third in franchise history with the pick. Levi Drake Rodriguez had two sacks, his first multi-sack game. Minnesota forced four turnovers in all.

stories.text: 8: sacks of Jordan Love at Lambeau Field
stories.summary: Six different Vikings had one sack each, and Rodriguez added two. Love was pressured on 21 of 35 dropbacks and Green Bay managed 56 rushing yards. Minnesota also controlled the ball for more than 35 minutes.

stories.text: At 49ers in Mexico City Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: San Francisco is the home team, with the game played at Estadio Banorte. The Vikings will be without Addison and face the altitude. Watch how Cousins and Justin Jefferson, who drew a season-high 13 targets last week, adjust.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons use bye to tear the offense apart

stories.text: Stefanski keeps Rees calling plays through the bye
stories.summary: Coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed Monday that Tommy Rees stays on as play-caller after a 35-13 loss to Kansas City left Atlanta 3-7. Stefanski would not say how much confidence he has in Rees and promised a full review of the offensive process during the bye. Fans booed the offense at home, and running back Bijan Robinson said it was deserved.

stories.text: Bye week gives Atlanta time to heal, with two on IR
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson Jr. and outside linebacker Samson Ebukam are on injured reserve with hamstring injuries and can be activated one week after the bye. Receiver Zachariah Branch missed the last two games with a hamstring problem. Linebacker Divine Deablo sat out the Chiefs game with a forearm injury.

stories.text: Penix has thrown six picks in three games
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. has gone 51 of 98 for 573 yards, one touchdown and six interceptions over the last three games. Four of those picks came in bad weather against Tampa Bay. The offense led the league in scoring through his first five starts, but it has scored 30 points total in the last three.

stories.text: 4: straight three-and-outs to open against Kansas City
stories.summary: Atlanta opened the Chiefs game with four straight three-and-outs, something the franchise had not done since 2000. The Falcons had 186 net yards through three quarters. They gained 184 more in the fourth, after the game was decided.

stories.text: Bye in Week 11, then a trip to Minnesota
stories.summary: Atlanta is off this week. The Falcons meet and lift Monday and Tuesday, and players get the rest of the week off. They return Nov. 29 at the 7-2 Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium. Watch whether Stefanski changes the offensive process he promised to review.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers take the NFC South lead on a last-second kick

stories.text: Fitzgerald's 54-yarder lifts Panthers into first place
stories.summary: Ryan Fitzgerald hit a 54-yard field goal as time expired to beat New Orleans 20-17 and give Carolina sole possession of the NFC South at 4-5. A 30-yard pass interference call on the Saints set up the winning drive. The lead changed hands twice in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Brooks, Horn and Jackson close to returning
stories.summary: Running back Jonathon Brooks and cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are close to returning, per the AJC's NFC South rundown. Receiver Xavier Legette played in Week 10. Linebacker Jaelan Phillips came back from a three-game hamstring absence against the Saints.

stories.text: Hubbard carries the load against New Orleans
stories.summary: Chuba Hubbard ran 27 times for 92 yards and caught five passes for 80 yards. He touched the ball on every snap of the winning drive except for the quarterback and center. Bryce Young finished 17 of 30 for 200 yards.

stories.text: 17: penalties, a franchise record
stories.summary: Carolina was flagged 17 times for 152 yards against the Saints, a franchise record, and still won. A horse-collar penalty on Phillips set up a Saints touchdown in the fourth quarter. The defense held New Orleans to 2.1 yards per carry and had three sacks.

stories.text: Ravens visit Charlotte on Sunday
stories.summary: Carolina hosts the 4-6 Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX at Bank of America Stadium. The Panthers lead the division by a game over Tampa Bay and 1.5 over Atlanta. Watch whether the penalty count drops.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints lose on a kick as time runs out

stories.text: Saints fall 20-17 on the final play at home
stories.summary: Charlie Smyth tied the game with a 55-yard field goal with 41 seconds left, but Carolina answered with a 54-yarder at the gun. New Orleans is 3-6 and 1-4 at home. Coach Kellen Moore said the offense needs to be more aggressive and find ways to move the ball downfield.

stories.text: Werner and Richards hurt, McCoy out
stories.summary: Linebacker Pete Werner left the Carolina game in the first half with a hamstring strain, and right tackle Asim Richards went out in the second half with a knee injury. Center Erik McCoy is out with a biceps injury. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. returned after a seven-week absence and ran eight times for 14 yards.

stories.text: Rookie Jordyn Tyson catches 11 passes in game two
stories.summary: Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in his second NFL game. Tyler Shough went 25 of 35 for 187 yards with one touchdown and one interception, and was the team's leading rusher with 25 yards on six carries.

stories.text: 107: first-half yards for the Saints
stories.summary: New Orleans managed just 107 yards of offense in the first half against Carolina and turned the ball over twice before the Panthers scored. The Saints rushed for 49 yards on the day. Alvin Kamara scored on his first touch of the game, a 3-yard run in the third quarter.

stories.text: Saints head to Chicago to face Caleb Williams
stories.summary: New Orleans visits the Bears on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX at Soldier Field. Chicago is 7-2 and has won four straight. Watch whether the Saints can move the ball downfield after rushing for just 49 yards against Carolina.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Mayfield's ankle clouds Sunday at Detroit

stories.text: Mayfield uncertain for Sunday's game in Detroit
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield has a foot and ankle injury from the Week 9 loss to Chicago and has been in and out of a walking boot. Sources told ESPN the injury is not long-term and injured reserve is not being considered. No one has ruled him out, and the question is pain tolerance. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels would start if Mayfield cannot go.

stories.text: Mayfield questionable, Diaby may return
stories.summary: Mayfield is listed questionable with a foot sprain. Tampa Bay promoted Easton Stick to the active roster and signed Cooper Rush to the practice squad. Edge rusher YaYa Diaby, who has a Grade 2 hamstring strain, may return this week.

stories.text: Bucky Irving runs for 97 yards against Chicago
stories.summary: Bucky Irving carried 20 times for 97 yards and two touchdowns in the 27-24 loss to the Bears. His second score tied the game at 24 with 2:51 left. Tampa Bay ran for 126 yards as a team to Chicago's 72.

stories.text: 21: takeaways, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay's defense leads the league with 21 takeaways, 16 of them interceptions. The Bucs have forced four or more turnovers in three straight games, a franchise record. The passing offense ranks 32nd in the league.

stories.text: Bucs travel to face the 7-2 Lions
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1:00 p.m. ET at Ford Field. The team's own game page lists FOX as the local broadcast. Linebacker Alex Anzalone says the Bucs must stop Jahmyr Gibbs and the run first. Tampa Bay then hosts Carolina on Monday Night Football on Nov. 30.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Home losing streak hits 11 games

stories.text: Cardinals' home losing streak reaches 11 games after 34-6 loss to Rams
stories.summary: Arizona has not won at home in 427 days. Only three more losses would tie the NFL record of 14 straight, set by the 1988 to 1989 Cowboys and the 2008 to 2010 Rams. Five home games remain: Commanders, Eagles, Jets, Raiders and 49ers.

stories.text: Minshew and Burch done for the year, Love on IR
stories.summary: Quarterback Gardner Minshew is expected to need season-ending surgery on a torn UCL. Defensive end Jordan Burch will miss the rest of the season with an MCL injury. Wide receivers Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) are also out for the year, and running back Jeremiyah Love is on IR with a high ankle sprain.

stories.text: Rookie QB Carson Beck takes his first NFL lumps
stories.summary: Beck was the third-string emergency quarterback two weeks ago. He went 11 of 18 for 103 yards with two interceptions against Los Angeles and took five sacks. Coach Mike LaFleur said neither pick was Beck's fault and that the final seven weeks are a roster evaluation.

stories.text: 34: Arizona ran just 34 offensive plays, a franchise low
stories.summary: The Cardinals gained 123 total yards and ran for only 34 against the Rams. The 34 plays are the fewest in franchise history, a sign of how little the offense sustained after the opening quarter.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Chiefs on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona travels to GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22. Watch whether Beck gets any help from a patched-up offensive line against a loud road crowd.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Four straight wins heading into the bye

stories.text: Rams win fourth straight, crush Cardinals 34-6 before bye
stories.summary: Los Angeles trailed 6-3 late in the second quarter, then scored twice in the final 1:06 of the first half to lead 17-6 at the break. The Rams improved to 6-4 and now rest during Week 11.

stories.text: Two centers hurt, Nacua and Adams sat out
stories.summary: Puka Nacua and Davante Adams missed the Arizona game. Centers Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and Dylan McMahon (knee) both went out in the first half, so Beaux Limmer moved from left guard to center and Bill Murray stepped in at guard. The bye gives the line time to heal.

stories.text: Blake Corum runs for 100 yards and a score
stories.summary: Corum carried 17 times for 100 yards and a 1-yard touchdown. It was his second 100-yard game of the season, and it came while the Rams played without their top two receivers.

stories.text: 9: Different Rams caught a Matthew Stafford pass
stories.summary: Stafford went 18 of 26 for 249 yards and three touchdowns, spreading the ball across nine targets. Tyler Higbee, Xavier Smith and Davis Allen each caught a touchdown pass.

stories.text: Rams on bye, then Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
stories.summary: Los Angeles is off in Week 11. The Rams return to face Green Bay on Wednesday, Nov. 25, with only nine days of rest instead of the usual 13. Watch the health of the interior line and the Nacua and Adams timeline.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Purdy and McCaffrey torch Dallas in 46-40 win

stories.text: 49ers outlast Cowboys 46-40 to reach 8-1
stories.summary: San Francisco gained 584 yards and scored six touchdowns in a Sunday shootout at AT&T Stadium. The win was the 49ers' fifth straight over Dallas and keeps them at the top of the NFC.

stories.text: Mason, Samuel, Winters and Green all banged up
stories.summary: Running back Jordan Mason re-injured his shoulder and did not play in the second half. Deebo Samuel left in the fourth quarter with a rib injury, linebacker Dee Winters suffered a concussion on kickoff coverage, and rookie cornerback Renardo Green hurt his ankle. Kyle Shanahan gave no long-term prognoses.

stories.text: Christian McCaffrey piles up 223 scrimmage yards and three TDs
stories.summary: McCaffrey caught four passes for 161 yards, including a 74-yard touchdown that was the longest of his career, and added 62 rushing yards on 13 carries. Brock Purdy threw to him all night in a 22-of-28, 389-yard, three-touchdown game.

stories.text: 389: Brock Purdy's passing yards with no interceptions
stories.summary: Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for three touchdowns and a 154.5 passer rating. Keenan Allen added five catches for 61 yards in his 49ers debut.

stories.text: 49ers face Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: San Francisco (8-1) meets Minnesota (7-2) at Estadio Azteca on Nov. 22 in the NFL's last international game of 2026. The team trains in Colorado Springs first. Watch the injury report for Samuel and Mason.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Smith-Njigba's historic year, bye at 6-4

stories.text: Seahawks beat Raiders 21-13 and head into bye at 6-4
stories.summary: Seattle trailed 10-7 at halftime, then never trailed after the third quarter began. Drew Lock, starting while Sam Darnold is hurt, went 14 of 17 for 240 yards and two touchdowns and is 3-0 as a starter. The Seahawks sacked rookie Fernando Mendoza six times.

stories.text: Darnold expected back, Lucas and Holani hurt vs. Raiders
stories.summary: Coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold the starter and said the team is optimistic he will get a full week of practice. Right tackle Abraham Lucas (ankle) and running back George Holani (knee) left the Raiders game and did not return. The bye gives both time to heal.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the only 1,000-yard receiver in the NFL
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba caught eight passes for 171 yards and a touchdown against Las Vegas. Through 10 games he has 79 catches for 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns, and he accounts for 52 percent of Seattle's receiving yards. CeeDee Lamb is next at 976 yards.

stories.text: 144: Smith-Njigba's receiving yards in one quarter, a team record
stories.summary: He piled up 144 yards in the third quarter alone against the Raiders, a Seahawks franchise record for a single quarter. It included a 71-yard touchdown catch from Lock.

stories.text: Seahawks on bye, then at the 49ers on Nov. 29
stories.summary: Seattle is off in Week 11. The Seahawks return to visit the NFC West-leading 49ers (8-1) on Nov. 29. Watch whether Darnold is back under center and how the right side of the line holds up.
